artworks.title: Cyrene and Cattle
artworks.description: Calvert's pastoral panel shows Apollo's Thessalian lover at rest among her father's cattle — the hunting nymph of Peneus whom the god would carry to Libya and who bore him Aristaeus, the keeper of bees and herds in Apollonius' Argonautica.

artworks.title: Mosaic of the nymph Cyrene
artworks.description: A North African floor mosaic from Lambaesis names Cyrene as a nymph — a provincial image of the Libyan figure Apollo set among the western nymphs, the same country that received her after the abduction from Haemonia.
